quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What should you do if there is a deep puddle on the road ahead?

options.text: Keep your speed the same to drive through the water.
Avoid the puddle if possible.
Shift into neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if possible.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles. These can cause your car to skid. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog shows that a pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must always yield the right-of-way to them.

questions.question: The center line has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line next to your lane. What does this mean?

options.text: You are not allowed to pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.
questions.explanation: When a solid line is next to the other lane and a broken line is next to your lane, you can pass. The broken line shows passing is allowed on your side.

questions.question: What should you do when a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane crosses the street?

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross the street.
You only need to yield the right-of-way at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog shows that a pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must always give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle loses traction due to water on the road?

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to gain traction.
Brake hard to stop your vehicle from sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When your tires lose contact with the road and ride on water (hydroplaning), slow down gradually. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the skid worse.

questions.question: What color and shape are construction zone signs?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. They are placed on the right side of the road, or on both sides if the road is divided.

questions.question: What speed should you drive when merging onto the freeway?

options.text: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
The posted speed limit for the freeway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, match the speed of traffic to merge safely.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
A curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of an upcoming curve to the right.

questions.question: What is the correct way to make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the centerline.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb.
Approach from the right lane, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb.
questions.explanation: Signal to other drivers. Slow down and stay as close to the right curb as possible when turning right.

questions.question: How should you avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep looking at the centerline of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid bright lights. Then continue checking the other vehicle's position.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you arrive at the intersection.
Turn your front wheels to the left to prepare for the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you arrive at the intersection.
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before turning. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: What does an orange and red triangular sign on a vehicle mean?

options.text: The vehicle has the right-of-way.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Shoulder work ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles like tractors and road maintenance vehicles display this orange and red triangle on the back.

questions.question: What does a red arrow pointing right on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You can turn in that direction after slowing and checking traffic.
You cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
You can turn in that direction after a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must wait until a green light or green arrow appears. Never turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: When should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often to see traffic moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see traffic moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors frequently while driving. This helps you know where other vehicles are near you.

questions.question: What should you do when entering traffic from a parked position at the curb?

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a gap large enough to reach the speed of traffic.
Wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough to reach the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap that lets you get up to the speed of other vehicles.

questions.question: You have a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Don't enter until you can drive completely across.
Drive into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't enter until you can drive completely across.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, only enter the intersection if you can cross completely before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: Is it legal to drive under the influence of medication that impairs your driving?

options.text: Never.
Yes, if you don't feel drowsy.
Yes, if a doctor prescribed it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance that impairs your driving. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: What should you do at intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings?

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed with caution.
Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At places where people may cross or traffic meets, look left and right to make sure no one is coming into your path.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road construction or maintenance area.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is displayed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do if you see pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Move to the right and go around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until the intersection is clear before driving through.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A yield sign is ahead.
A road is entering from the left.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yield sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is coming. Start to slow down when you see this warning sign.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Look straight ahead at the road.
Only watch the middle of the road.
Watch the sides, ahead, and behind your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the sides, ahead, and behind your car.
questions.explanation: A good driver watches all around their vehicle. You need to know what is happening in front, to the sides, and behind you at all times.

questions.question: If you want to pass a pedestrian on the road but an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.
questions.explanation: Handle one road hazard at a time. If you want to pass a pedestrian and an oncoming car is coming, slow down and wait for the car to pass. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: When passing a large truck, you should:

options.text: Move back to your lane and slow down right away.
Give the truck plenty of space before moving back to your lane.
Move back to your lane whenever you want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the truck plenty of space before moving back to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not move back to your lane too quickly after passing a large truck. Wait until you can see the entire front of the truck in your mirror before changing lanes. Do not slow down. Trucks need almost twice as much space as cars to stop.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Frustrate drivers about slow traffic.
Slow down drivers.
Keep traffic away from dangerous work zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic away from dangerous work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. These warn you and show you how to drive through the work zone safely.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant in any amount. It slows your nerves and body functions. It reduces your self-control and makes it harder to focus and stay alert.

questions.question: Trucks' blind spots are:

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the left side of the cab.
Both on the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both on the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Truck blind spots are much larger than car blind spots. The driver cannot see your car behind them. If you drive too close behind a truck, you cannot see traffic ahead. If the driver cannot see your face in their side mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection at the posted speed when the light turns yellow. You should:

options.text: Slow down and go through without caution.
Speed up to cross before the red light.
Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Stop at a yellow light if you can do so safely. Otherwise, go through the intersection carefully.

questions.question: You are in a minor collision at an intersection with no injuries and little damage. You should:

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if possible.
Never move your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if possible.
questions.explanation: After a collision, if no one is hurt and you can safely move your vehicle, move it out of the traffic lane.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep driving at your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be alert and drive carefully. Slow down when you see this light.

questions.question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic means:

options.text: Both lanes are going in the same direction.
You can pass when it is safe.
You cannot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A dashed yellow line separates traffic going in opposite directions. You can pass if no oncoming traffic is in the passing lane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road is changing direction or narrowing.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is changing direction or narrowing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a change in direction or a narrower road ahead. You may see these signs on sharp curves or near narrow bridges.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.

options.text: White
Blue
Green

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic movement. They are usually white with black markings and drivers must obey them.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are:

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about traffic laws. They may show rules about direction, lane use, turning, speed, parking, or special situations. These signs are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green letters or symbols.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic:

options.text: Only watch the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and make other vehicles move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, check to the side and behind your vehicle. Make sure no vehicles are in your way.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm out and red lights flashing, you should:

options.text: Stop completely and wait.
Honk before passing on the left side.
Keep driving after a few children get off the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait.
questions.explanation: When a school bus stops with its stop arm out and red lights flashing, come to a complete stop. Stay stopped until the arm is pulled in and the lights turn off.

questions.question: If you must park in an unusual location:

options.text: Leave your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: You must make sure your parked vehicle is not a hazard. Park where drivers approaching from any direction can see your car.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. You should:

options.text: Slow down before you enter the curve.
Slow to the freeway speed limit.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You may not see what is ahead, and braking in a curve can cause you to skid.

questions.question: What does a yellow left arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Get ready to let oncoming traffic go.
The protected left turn is ending.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means the protected left turn is about to end. Get ready to give the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When should drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave first.
Only if pedestrians are not using their phones.
Always.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle completely at a crosswalk to let any pedestrian cross. You can go only when your path is completely clear.
